$comment: These are regression-safety budgets for deterministic headless browser journeys, not product SLAs.
They intentionally detect hangs, missing output, interaction breakage, and extreme instability.
They must never be used to claim performance superiority over another SDK.
schemaVersion 2 (issue #562) adds staged scale-tier metrics, a 100k/1M row scale corpus, and repeated
mount/unmount + context-loss recovery leak budgets. BOTH scale tiers (deckgl.scale-render-100k and
deckgl.scale-render-1m) are opt-in (HONUA_BROWSER_BENCH_SCALE=full / npm run bench:browser:full-scale) and
excluded from the deterministic PR lane's default `npm run bench:browser` run; only the 10k
deckgl.binary-render-interact scenario, the capability scenarios, and the lifecycle scenarios run there.
The 100k entries below were calibrated from a real LOCAL Chromium+swiftshader run, then proved wrong on a
real CI run of the same tier (render 2677.80 ms / interaction 695 ms / gpuUpload 990 ms / steadyFps 1.3 —
well past these numbers): CI's software GL is not the same runner class as any given contributor's
machine, so a same-box baseline is not a portable CI budget. Treat every number in deckgl.scale-render-100k
and deckgl.scale-render-1m below as UNCALIBRATED FOR CI. The scheduled/manual deck.gl Full-Scale Evidence
workflow now captures HONUA_BROWSER_BENCH_SCALE=full reports on a stable Ubuntu runner class. Replace these
placeholders only after repeated reports establish runner variance. swiftshader is a CPU software rasterizer,
so its fill-rate-bound circle redraw is far slower than a real GPU (observed ~1 fps steady-state at 100k
points locally, worse on CI) — do not read these as real-device performance either way. The 1M budgets are
further extrapolated from the (already CI-invalidated) 100k baseline and are even less trustworthy.
stage metrics ending in Ms are upper bounds (smaller is better); steadyFrameRateFps is a lower bound
(direction: at-least) since a smaller frames-per-second value is the regression.
